# External or broad scouting

Use broader discovery only when repository-local evidence is insufficient.

Examples:
- upstream source/reference implementation;
- official framework documentation;
- generated code ownership;
- dependency behavior;
- related repositories explicitly in scope.

## Workflow

1. State the missing question.
2. Prefer authoritative/project-connected sources.
3. Search only enough to locate the relevant implementation/specification.
4. Return the exact source/version and what it establishes.
5. Keep interpretation separate from source fact.

Do not broaden to unrelated repositories merely because names are similar.

If external tools are unavailable, record the gap and continue with local evidence that remains useful.
